parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A rock of mass $7.5\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards from the surface of a planet. The rock leaves the surface of the planet with a speed of $4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at time $t = 0$. The variation with time $t$ of the velocity $v$ of the rock is shown in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1

Assume that the planet does not have an atmosphere and that the viscous force acting on the rock is always zero.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Determine the height of the rock above the surface of the planet at time $t = 4.0\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the change in the momentum of the rock from time $t = 0$ to time $t = 4.0\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the weight $W$ of the rock on this planet.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
In practice, the planet in (b) does have an atmosphere that causes a viscous force to act on the moving rock.

State and explain the variation, if any, in the resultant force acting on the rock as it moves vertically upwards.
